I found Voat several months ago when someone posted an AskReddit asking what other websites people like to visit and Snapzu and Voat were mentioned a few times, but at that time I didn't actually join Voat.

A week ago or so I saw someone mention it again and decided to come on over. Despite the obvious problems on Reddit, I don't hate it. I spend most of my time on a handful of smaller subs or in a few humour subs, so all the politics and stuff about 'SJWs' hasn't really affected me the way it has some other Voaters.

Mainly what I disliked about Reddit was that with so many people it's hard to be seen. Comments you make are immediately buried under an avalanche of dozens of puns, memes, inside jokes, obscure Reddit references and bullshit stories from liars. And there's a strange culture on Reddit to just downvote any new submissions. I actually don't know how anything gets to the frontpage, because in my experience no matter how relevant your post is to the subreddit you put it in or how inoffensive your question or information is it just immediately gets a handful of downvotes and no replies.

I like that Voat is quieter and there are more actual comments and less attention-seeking shitposting. Plus, I like that with a smaller crowd I get to see the same usernames over and over and get a sense for who people are and what they like.

Subs I'm interested in are any about films, comics, books, video games, science and history.
I don't hate reddit; I just prefer a smaller crowd

Sophie Turner (Sansa Stark) defends brutal scenes from 'Black Wedding': 'I kind of loved it'

I'm reading that a lot of people are leaving the show because this scene "wasn't necessary," but even as a feminist I completely disagree with them. Very few of the deaths and maimings in GoT are necessary, and making a big deal out of a rape while ignoring the whole other pile of atrocities that happen is exceptionalism. Anyone who could be negatively affected by accidentally viewing a rape scene should really know better than to watch GoT anyway.

If you want to argue that the amount of violence in GoT is obscene, then I won't agree, but that argument does at least make sense from certain perspectives. Saying there's too much of one of the most common types of violence is kind of ridiculous.

Further, this entire plotline is new, so even book readers don't know if this scene was necessary. What if she ends up conceiving a Bolton and we get a whole new plot line? And sure, we already knew Ramsay was evil, but Sansa didn't, not really. They had to establish that to her in a way that would break through the wall of ice she's had to build around her emotional self.

I suspect that anyone "leaving" because of that scene either didn't watch regularly, or didn't watch at all and just likes to complain on Twitter. Anyone who's seen the show and cared would have left long ago with scenes like Khal Drogo raping Daenerys while tears streamed down her face.

I was actually surprised at how subdued the Sansa rape scene was - partially because of bad writing (Reek crying in the corner for no reason, rather than being involved) - and partially because of Sophie Turner's obvious no-nudity clause in her contract. I'm not saying I want gruesome rape scenes - but the tameness actually seemed pretty out of place compared to normal GoT fare.
